body:
You are a dialogue writer for a single-player dark-fantasy RPG based on Curse of Strahd, set in the gloomy, mist-bound valley of Barovia. Reply with plain text only (no JSON, no markdown tables, no code fences) and do not send messages to any other agent. Write only what is asked, with no commentary before or after.

TONE: gothic horror with dry, understated, character-driven humour. Castle Ravenloft is the lord's house, three centuries old in its present state: dust, cold stone, candles that burn without being lit, a household of ghosts and the dead who keep small duties. The Narrator is an unseen storyteller who speaks to the party in second person, present tense, one or two sentences a line. Funny comes from specifics and deadpan, never from winking at the player. No modern slang, no pop culture, no real-world references. Where a scene is frightening, let it be frightening; where it is sad, let it be sad.

STYLE SAMPLES from the existing game (match this voice, length and rhythm):
Narrator: A long gallery lined with carved stone faces, and at the far end a fire burning in a great hearth.
Narrator: A portrait of a stern man in armour. Its eyes are not painted on. They follow you.
Narrator: A saint carved in white stone, hands open. Her face has been cut away with care, the way you'd peel fruit.
Narrator: A stone bench facing the view, its seat worn hollow by someone who sat here a great deal.
Narrator: The great doors swing inward before you touch them, and close behind you just as quietly.
Narrator: A guard post with arrow slits and an empty weapon stand. Whoever stood here left a long time ago.

OUTPUT FORMAT: for each label below write the label on its own line (like "== entry_dragon_look"), then each line on its own line as `Narrator: text`. Every line is spoken by the Narrator. Do not number the lines.

RULES FOR EVERY LINE: under 190 characters, usually 60 to 130; no braces or placeholders; no em dashes (use commas, full stops or colons); no real-world references; straight apostrophes and quotes; each line should make sense on its own, and a label's lines read in order as a short scene. Never name or describe the player characters individually (say "you" or "the party"). Do not state game numbers (no hit points, no damage dice, no difficulty numbers, no feet except where a label says so).

SETTING NOTES (stay inside these, invent nothing about Barovia's history beyond them):
- The entry hall is the first room inside the castle's great doors. It is cold marble with a long rug. Small stone dragons, child-sized, crouch on plinths and ledges overlooking it. Nobody remarks on them. They stay still while you walk in and begin to stir only when you turn to leave.
- South of the dining hall, behind a panel set into the wall, is the archers' post: a narrow room with arrow slits and bow racks. The count had every mirror in the castle taken down and put away here (he casts no reflection), so tall mirrors stand along the walls, some face to the wall, some under dust sheets.
- The passage to the chapel is lined with statues of knights in plate, hands on sword hilts. Their eyes seem to follow you as you walk past. It is an optical illusion: the eyes are carved as shallow hollows, which an old mason's trick makes seem to turn. Nothing supernatural.
- The king's balcony is a private gallery above the chapel where the lord worshipped. It has two high thrones. Two shambling dead sit slumped in them as an ambush and rise when someone comes near. A narrow stair climbs to it from the chapel with one landing whose boards creak loudly under any step.
- The castle's overlook is a long balcony on its flank over a cliff. Far below, 110 feet down the cliff face, is a window caked with dirt that is easy to miss. It lights the tomb of King Barov and Queen Ravenovia, the lord's parents: two coffins side by side, a gold mosaic on the ceiling, tall stained windows. A person could climb down to it with a rope or by hand, and in the tomb they would land among the coffins.

LABELS AND BEATS:
== entry_dragon_look
Examining one of the little stone dragons in the entry hall. 2 Narrator lines.
== entry_dragons_wake
The party turns toward the great doors to leave, and the stone dragons wake, stretching, stone grinding. 4 Narrator lines, the last one a fearful cold sentence that can open a fight.
== entry_dragon_rubble
Looking at the broken pieces of a stone dragon after the fight. 1 Narrator line.
== archers_post_enter
The party steps through the hidden panel into the archers' post and sees the mirrors. 3 Narrator lines.
== post_mirror_look
Looking at one of the mirrors, standing with its glass to the room. 3 Narrator lines, the last about the count and reflections.
== post_mirror_turned
A mirror turned to face the wall, its back bare wood. 2 Narrator lines.
== post_rack
The bow racks, empty. 1 Narrator line.
== faith_knights_look
Looking at the knight statues in the chapel passage as their eyes seem to follow. 3 Narrator lines.
== faith_knights_trick
Someone works out the trick: the eyes are shallow carved hollows. 2 Narrator lines.
== faith_knights_miss
Someone studies them and cannot tell why the eyes seem to move. 1 Narrator line.
== landing_creak
The party steps onto the creaking landing of the narrow stair to the king's balcony. 3 Narrator lines.
== balcony_enter
The party arrives on the king's balcony: the dark chapel below, two high thrones, two slumped figures. 3 Narrator lines.
== balcony_throne_look
Looking at one of the empty high thrones. 2 Narrator lines.
== balcony_zombies_rise
The two slumped figures in the thrones rise as the party comes near. 2 Narrator lines, the second can open a fight.
== window_found
Searching at the overlook's parapet, the party spots the dirt-caked window far below on the cliff face. 3 Narrator lines.
== window_climb_rope
Climbing down the cliff face on a rope to the window. 3 Narrator lines.
== window_climb_bare
Climbing down the bare rock by hand, a hard climb. 3 Narrator lines.
== window_climb_slip
A hand slips on the way down and the climber catches a ledge, bruised. 2 Narrator lines.
== window_tomb_landing
Dropping through the window into the tomb of King Barov and Queen Ravenovia. 3 Narrator lines.
result:
== entry_dragon_look
Narrator: A stone dragon the size of a child crouches on the high ledge, wings folded tight against its ribs.
Narrator: Its claws are cut deep into the marble plinth, as if it were afraid of being blown away.
== entry_dragons_wake
Narrator: As you turn back toward the great doors, a dry grinding sound echoes from the ledges above.
Narrator: Dust spills from the ceiling as the little stone dragons uncurl their tails and stretch their cramped wings.
Narrator: They have waited very patiently for you to come in, and they have no intention of letting you leave.
Narrator: Four pairs of grey stone eyes fix on your backs, and the things drop from their perches.
== entry_dragon_rubble
Narrator: Chunks of grey stone lie scattered across the marble floor, looking no different from any other broken masonry.
== archers_post_enter
Narrator: The wooden panel swings aside to reveal a narrow guard room smelling of old dust and dry linen.
Narrator: Arrow slits pierce the outer wall, though no bowman could easily stand at them now.
Narrator: Every spare inch of the room is crowded with tall mirrors, some draped in grey sheets and others facing the stone.
== post_mirror_look
Narrator: You lift the corner of a heavy dust sheet and find yourself staring into tarnished silver glass.
Narrator: The frame is gilded oak, fine enough for a state bedroom, left here to rot in the dark.
Narrator: The master of the house casts no reflection, and it seems he grew tired of glass that only showed him empty rooms.
== post_mirror_turned
Narrator: This mirror has been stood with its face pressed flat against the cold masonry, showing only its bare wooden backing.
Narrator: Whoever carried it in here did not even want the wall to look at itself.
== post_rack
Narrator: The wooden racks meant for longbows stand bare, their pegs polished smooth by hands now three centuries dead.
== faith_knights_look
Narrator: Armed knights in full plate stand along both walls of the passage, their stone hands resting on their sword hilts.
Narrator: As you walk between them, their visored heads seem to turn by slow degrees to watch you pass.
Narrator: Even when you stop dead in your tracks, you feel their cold gaze lingering on the back of your neck.
== faith_knights_trick
Narrator: Looking closer at the visor, you see the eyes are not rounded at all, but carved as shallow, concave hollows.
Narrator: It is an old mason's trick of light and shadow: there is no ghost in the stone, only clever chisel work.
== faith_knights_miss
Narrator: You stare back into the visor until your eyes water, yet you cannot tell how the stone manages to follow you.
== landing_creak
Narrator: Your boot comes down on the narrow landing, and the dry floorboards let out a long, sharp groan.
Narrator: In the dead quiet of the chapel, the sound carries like a dropped tray of ironware.
Narrator: If anything waits in the gallery above, it knows you are coming.
== balcony_enter
Narrator: The stair opens onto a private gallery overlooking the dark nave of the chapel far below.
Narrator: Two high-backed wooden thrones stand at the rail, where the lord of the castle once sat to hear his prayers.
Narrator: A figure sits slumped in each chair, heads bowed as if they fell asleep during a very long sermon.
== balcony_throne_look
Narrator: The high throne is carved from dark timber, its velvet cushion rotted through and stained by what last sat in it.
Narrator: From here, the lord could look down upon the altar without ever having to kneel among the congregation.
== balcony_zombies_rise
Narrator: As you step toward the rail, the two slumped corpses stiffen, wet cloth peeling away from the wood of the thrones.
Narrator: They rise together in dead silence, dry jaws hanging open, and reach for your throats.
== window_found
Narrator: Leaning out over the low parapet, you peer down the sheer rock of the cliff into the swirling mist.
Narrator: More than a hundred feet straight down, a tall lancet window is set directly into the mountain stone.
Narrator: Its glass is so thick with old grime and swallow droppings that it blends almost completely into the crag.
== window_climb_rope
Narrator: You make the rope fast to the cold stone of the parapet and let the coil drop into the mist below.
Narrator: Bracing your boots against the cliff face, you walk yourself backward down the rock, hand over hand.
Narrator: The wind tugs at your cloak as the castle wall rises above you and the dirty glass draws near.
== window_climb_bare
Narrator: You swing your legs over the parapet and hunt with your boots for the first narrow seam in the rock.
Narrator: The stone is damp with mist and slick under your fingers, offering only shallow cracks and cold ledges.
Narrator: With the drop yawning beneath your heels, you work your way down the cliff one careful inch at a time.
== window_climb_slip
Narrator: Your fingers skitter off a patch of wet lichen, and for one sickening heartbeat you are falling.
Narrator: You slam hard against a lower ledge and catch hold with bruised ribs and scraped knuckles, breathing fast.
== window_tomb_landing
Narrator: You pry the grimy casement open and drop through, your boots ringing loud against a floor of cold stone.
Narrator: Above you, a ceiling of tarnished gold mosaic glimmers dimly in the grey light filtering through tall stained glass.
Narrator: You have landed squarely between two white marble coffins, where King Barov and Queen Ravenovia lie side by side.
